title: ai trading bot
author: Cool_Big2955
selftext: im building a fully functional adaptive trading bot where users can customize all thresholds directly in the .env file instead of being locked into fixed settings the system uses dynamic work zones based on 48h price boxes combined with t-weighted win rates to automatically adjust rsi entries and hard stops so it adapts to changing volatility without manual intervention im curious how many people here would actually be interested in buying a self-adjusting bot like this where you retain full control over the risk parameters rather than relying on a black box ai that promises unrealistic returns

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the self-adjusting part is what I'd worry about. thresholds that retune off their own recent hits will look brilliant in any backtest, because they're fitted to the same data they're scored on. run it forward untouched for a month before asking anyone to pay. I built Quantradin as a place to do that run, live prices and fake money. quantradin.com.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Letting users see and control every threshold is a better selling point than a black box. Before selling it, though, I'd have a forward track record to show, since a self-adjusting bot that retunes from recent win rates can chase noise. The adjustment rule itself needs testing on data it never saw, with costs, and the number of trades behind each adjustment should be shown. Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for macro releases) is one source you could use to check how the adaptive settings behave around news.
